Structure Examples Instructions Operands Methods Limits

IJVM Instructions

The reduced IJVM instruction set that the interpreter runs. Instructions that are not on this page are not supported.

Program structure

Sections go in this order. Directives are lower case: .MAIN is an error.

SectionContent
.constant ... .end-constantOptional. One constant per line: NAME value.
.main ... .end-mainRequired. The main program.
.method name(p1, p2) ... .end-methodOptional, one per method. The method ends with IRETURN.
.var ... .end-varAt the start of .main or of a method. One local variable per line.
  • A label is name: on a line by itself. L1: BIPUSH 1 is a syntax error.
  • Names can contain -, for example end-while.
  • Comments start with // or with ;.
  • Instructions work in upper or lower case.
  • Variable names are case-sensitive. Constant names are not.

Examples for your first run

Create a .ijvm file, copy an example into the file and click Run or Debug.

1. Hello

hello.ijvm
.main
    BIPUSH 72       // 'H'
    OUT
    BIPUSH 101      // 'e'
    OUT
    BIPUSH 108      // 'l'
    OUT
    BIPUSH 108      // 'l'
    OUT
    BIPUSH 111      // 'o'
    OUT
    BIPUSH 10       // newline
    OUT
.end-main

Output: Hello

2. Input and output

The program adds two one-digit numbers. Each number ends with ;.

sum.ijvm
.main
    .var
        a
    .end-var
    IN              // first digit
    BIPUSH 48
    ISUB            // value = character - '0'
    ISTORE a
    IN              // ';'
    POP
    IN              // second digit
    BIPUSH 48
    ISUB
    ILOAD a
    IADD            // a + b
    BIPUSH 48
    IADD            // back to ASCII
    OUT
    IN              // ';'
    POP
.end-main

Input 3;4; → output 7. Type the input in the terminal and press Enter.

3. Method with INVOKEVIRTUAL

method.ijvm
.constant
    OBJREF 0x40
.end-constant

.main
    LDC_W OBJREF    // object reference, popped by INVOKEVIRTUAL
    BIPUSH 3        // a
    BIPUSH 4        // b
    INVOKEVIRTUAL add
    BIPUSH 48
    IADD            // result + '0'
    OUT
    HALT
.end-main

.method add(a, b)
    ILOAD a
    ILOAD b
    IADD
    IRETURN
.end-method

Output: 7, then the HALT summary. In Debug, the STACK shows the add() frame inside the main() frame.

Instructions

The stack contains words (integers). a is the word below the top, b is the word on top.

InstructionOperandsDescription
BIPUSHnumberPushes the number onto the stack.
DUP-Copies the top word and pushes the copy onto the stack.
ERR-Prints ERROR: the program executed ERR. and stops the program with code 1.
GOTOlabelJumps to the label.
HALT-Stops the program with code 0 and prints PROGRAM OUTPUT IS: followed by all the OUT characters.
IADD-Pops a and b, pushes a + b.
IAND-Pops a and b, pushes the bitwise AND.
IFEQlabelPops a word and jumps if the word is 0.
IFLTlabelPops a word and jumps if the word is less than 0.
IF_ICMPEQlabelPops two words and jumps if they are equal.
IINCvariable numberAdds the number to the variable. There is no comma: IINC i 1, IINC j -1.
ILOADvariablePushes the value of the variable onto the stack. The variable must have a value (ISTORE or parameter).
IN-Reads one input character and pushes its code (0 to 255) onto the stack. If the input is empty, the program waits: type the characters in the terminal and press Enter. Enter does not send the newline character.
INVOKEVIRTUALmethodCalls the method. Pops the arguments and then the object reference (OBJREF). See Methods.
IOR-Pops a and b, pushes the bitwise OR.
IRETURN-Pops the top value, ends the method and pushes the value onto the caller's stack.
ISTOREvariablePops a word and writes it into the variable.
ISUB-Pops a and b, pushes a - b. BIPUSH 9, BIPUSH 3, ISUB gives 6.
LDC_WconstantPushes the value of the constant onto the stack.
NOP-Does nothing.
OUT-Pops a word and prints the character with that code.
POP-Removes the top word.
SWAP-Swaps the two top words.

Operands

OperandDescription
numberDecimal (27, -1), hexadecimal (0x1B) or octal with the o prefix (o33). 027 is decimal and equals 27. Characters such as 'A' are not supported: use the code (65).
labelThe name of a label in the method.
variableThe name of a .var variable or of a method parameter.
methodThe name of a .method method.
constantThe name of a .constant constant.

Methods

  1. Push the object reference onto the stack. There is no predefined OBJREF: define a constant (for example OBJREF 0x40) and use LDC_W OBJREF, or push any word.
  2. Push the arguments onto the stack, in parameter order.
  3. Run INVOKEVIRTUAL method. The method receives the arguments in its parameters.
  4. The method ends with IRETURN. After the call, the return value is on top of the caller's stack.

A name cannot be used for both a variable and a method.

Differences from the textbook IJVM

Interpreter behaviors to be aware of
  • BIPUSH does not check the byte range: BIPUSH 300 pushes 300.
  • WIDE and INP are not supported.
  • If .main ends without HALT, the program finishes without the PROGRAM OUTPUT IS: summary.
